newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower, down seven percent on week.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower, down seven percent on week.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended weaker Friday after the market capitulated late in the day to persistent origin selling, trading sources said.
Arabica prices drifted on the plus side for most of the session, bolstered by steady buying from day traders and the roasting sector.

But the market reversed direction ahead of the closing bell, as price-fixing by key grower Colombia snarled an attempt to punch through chart resistance at 107-108 cents. Options-related selling also pressured the futures market, dealers said, noting keen interest in November and December calls at 110 cents.
"There was non-stop selling from Colombia all day long," said one trader.
Benchmark December fell 0.50 cent per lb on the day, to close at 104.70, a fresh one-month low. Spot September rose 0.40 cent, to 115.25, while the outer months eased 0.45 to 1.05.
The arabica market took a beating on the week, sliding seven percent as traders grew confident that the worst of this year's supply crunch had passed.
With the arrival of new-crop coffee seen just around the corner, dealers said the market appeared headed for a test of the crucial 100.00-cent ($1) per lb mark.

News that Brazil had approved a bill exempting commodities such as coffee from an export tax, the ICMS, further fueled this week's decline, they said, as the market braced itself for additional shipments from the world's top grower.
Tonight's CFTC Commitment of Traders reports may provide some additional direction, with dealers anticipating a decline in the hefty speculative long position.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
